page: Microsoft Azure D16as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv4 family, provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2 instruction sets, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Local storage includes a bundled 137 GB SSD, and there are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core reaching 2707.98 (top 25%) and a Geekbench single-core score of 1585.0. Multi-core performance is balanced in the median range, recording 21652.21 in stress-ng and 10387.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Memory throughput is substantial, evidenced by a PassMark memory score of 2783.85 (top 25%), small-block read speeds of 1040.39 GB/sec, and uncached large-block reads of 94.0 GB/sec. Application benchmarks show solid middle-tier capability, handling 16.26 million Redis SET operations per second and 14.32 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The instance delivers a balanced efficiency profile for enterprise systems that need consistent compute and reliable memory bandwidth without GPU acceleration. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC resources, 64 GB RAM, and bundled local SSD storage fits production web applications, relational databases, CI/CD compilation, and mid-tier caching infrastructure.

D16as_v4 fits general-purpose workloads, including web servers, backend database engines, caching tiers, and software build pipelines.
